chunks: He said: Abu Hafs Umar ibn Muhammad al-Sayrafi reported to me, saying: Abul Hasan Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Sufi reported to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Muti' reported to us, saying: Khalid ibn Abdillah reported to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from Atiyyah, from Ka'b al-Ahbar who said:
It is written in the Torah: Whoever does a good turn to a fool, it is a sin recorded against him.
And may Allah bless Muhammad and his pure and purified family, and send them greetings of peace.

key_terms.أحمق: Ahmaq - a fool, one lacking sound judgment
key_terms.التوراة: Torah - the holy book revealed to Prophet Musa (Moses)
key_terms.خطيئة: Khati'a - a sin, error, or transgression
key_terms.كعب الأحبار: Ka'b al-Ahbar - a Jewish scholar who embraced Islam, known for transmitting Isra'iliyyat
key_terms.معروف: Ma'ruf - a good deed, favor, or act of kindness

ai.seo_question: What does the Torah say about doing good to a foolish person?
ai.summary: This narration quotes Ka'b al-Ahbar, a Jewish scholar who converted to Islam, transmitting a wisdom found in the Torah. It warns that bestowing favors upon a foolish person is actually counted as a transgression, because the fool is unable to appreciate or properly use such kindness. The teaching was well-known in early Islamic scholarly circles that valued the concept of placing goodness where it is deserved.
